metrics.name: False Assurance Rate (FAR)
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of positive assurance decisions that were incorrect. Lower is better. 0.0 is ideal but trivially achieved by abstaining.
metrics.limitation: A system that always abstains achieves FAR=None (undefined). Must be read alongside Violation Recall and Correct Assurance Rate.
metrics.notes: False assurance count: 3. Positive assurance count: 4.

metrics.name: Violation Recall
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of true violations the system correctly identified. Higher is better. Must be read alongside FAR to prevent gaming.
metrics.limitation: A system that always returns VIOLATED achieves recall=1.0 while also having many false assurances for correct implementations.

metrics.name: Violation Precision
metrics.interpretation: Of all cases where the system said VIOLATED, what fraction actually were. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: A system that never predicts VIOLATED has precision=None. Must be read alongside Violation Recall.

metrics.name: Correct Positive Assurance Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of correct implementations that the system correctly assured. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: A system that always returns UNKNOWN achieves 0. Must be read alongside FAR.

metrics.name: Ambiguity Recall
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of genuinely ambiguous requirements that the system flagged as ambiguous. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: A system that always says ambiguous would achieve recall=1.0 at the cost of enormous false-positive ambiguity signals.

metrics.name: Contradiction Recall
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of contradictory requirements that the system surfaced. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: May be zero if the benchmark dataset has few contradiction cases.

metrics.name: Phantom Requirement Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of phantom requirements that were incorrectly treated as confirmed, producing positive assurance without human confirmation. Lower is better. 0.0 is ideal.
metrics.limitation: Requires at least one Category F case to be meaningful. May be undefined with zero F cases.

metrics.name: Stale Evidence Detection Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of stale-evidence cases where the system correctly declined to produce a positive assurance. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: Does not measure whether the system explicitly named the evidence as stale; only that it avoided a false positive assurance.

metrics.name: Semantic Drift Detection Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of semantic drift cases where the system triggered REVIEW or BLOCK. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: Requires Category Q cases to be meaningful. A system without drift analysis will score 0.

metrics.name: Counterexample Discovery Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of category J cases where the system proposed at least one counterexample. Higher is better. Note: proposed counterexamples are NOT confirmed violations.
metrics.limitation: A system can produce many invalid counterexamples and still score high. Counterexample precision is a future metric.

metrics.name: Appropriate Uncertainty Rate
metrics.interpretation: Proportion of cases expecting UNKNOWN/INCONCLUSIVE where the system correctly returned an uncertain verdict. Higher is better.
metrics.limitation: A system that always returns UNKNOWN scores 1.0 here but is useless overall. Must be read with Correct Positive Assurance Rate.
